The **iPhone**<sup>[\[a\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-7)</sup> is a [smartphone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smartphone) developed and marketed by [Apple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Inc.) as the first device in the [iPhone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPhone) lineup of smartphones. It features a [Samsung S5L8900](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_iPhone_systems-on-chip) SoC (90 nm), a 3.5 in [multi-touch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multi-touch) display, and a [web browser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_browser) ([Safari](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safari_(web_browser)>)). After years of rumors and speculation, it was officially announced on January 9, 2007, and was released in the United States on June 29, 2007.

[Development of the iPhone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_iPhone) began in 2005 and continued in secrecy until its public unveiling at [Macworld 2007](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macworld_2007). The device broke with prevailing mobile phone designs by eliminating most physical hardware buttons, and relying on a finger-friendly touchscreen interface that did not need a stylus. The iPhone featured [quad-band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quad-band) [GSM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GSM) cellular connectivity with [GPRS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPRS) and [EDGE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enhanced_Data_Rates_for_GSM_Evolution) support for [data transfer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_transfer), and it used continuous internet access and onboard processing to support features unrelated to voice communication.

The iPhone generated much hype before release<sup>[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-8)</sup> and quickly became Apple's most successful product, although it was met with less enthusiasm in European territories.<sup>[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-9)</sup> At the time, the iPhone appealed largely to the general public, as opposed to the business community, upon which [BlackBerry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BlackBerry) and [IBM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IBM) were primarily focused. By integrating existing technology and expanding on [usability](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Usability), the iPhone turned the smartphone industry "on its head",<sup>[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-10)</sup> and later generations of the iPhone propelled Apple to become one of the world's [most profitable companies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_companies_by_revenue).<sup>[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-OL-11)</sup> Its successor, the [iPhone 3G](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPhone_3G), was announced on June 9, 2008.

## Development history

In 2000, Apple CEO [Steve Jobs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Jobs) envisioned an Apple [touchscreen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Touchscreen) product that the user could interact with directly with their fingers rather than using a stylus.<sup>\[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed)*\]</sup> The stylus was a common tool for many existing touchscreen devices at the time including Apple's own [Newton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Newton), launched in 1993. He decided that the device would require a triple layered [capacitive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capacitive_touchscreen) [multi-touch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multi-touch) [touch screen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Touch_screen), a very new and advanced technology at the time. This helped with removing the physical [keyboard](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keyboard_(computing)>) and [mouse](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mouse_(computing)>). The same as was common at the time for [tablet computers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tablet_computer), human machine interfaces, and point of sale systems. Jobs recruited a group of Apple engineers to investigate the idea as a side project.<sup>[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-macworldlive-12)</sup> When Jobs reviewed the prototype and its [user interface](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_interface), he saw the potential in developing the concept into a mobile phone to compete with already established brands in the then emerging market for touch screen phones.<sup>[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-13)</sup> The whole effort was called Project Purple 2 and began in 2005.<sup>[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-14)</sup> Apple had purchased the "iphone.org" domain in December 1999.[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-15)

Apple created the device in a secretive and unprecedented collaboration with [Cingular Wireless](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AT&T_Mobility), now part of [AT&T](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AT&T). The development cost of the collaboration was estimated to have been $150 million<sup>[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-16)</sup> over a thirty-month period. Apple rejected the "[design by committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Design_by_committee)" approach that had yielded the [Motorola ROKR E1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motorola_ROKR_E1), a largely unsuccessful collaboration with [Motorola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motorola). Instead, Cingular Wireless gave Apple the liberty to develop the iPhone's hardware and software [in-house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In-house).[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-CNN_secrets-17)<sup>[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-18)</sup> The original iPhone was introduced by Steve Jobs on January 9, 2007, in a [keynote address](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stevenote) at the [Macworld Conference & Expo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macworld_Conference_&_Expo#2007) held in [Moscone West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscone_Center) in San Francisco, California.<sup>[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-macworldlive-12)</sup> In his address, Jobs said, "This is a day that I have been looking forward to for two and a half years," and that "today, Apple is going to reinvent the phone".<sup>[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-19)</sup> Jobs introduced the iPhone as a combination of three devices: a "widescreen [iPod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPod) with touch controls"; a "revolutionary mobile phone"; and a "breakthrough Internet communicator."[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-20)

Six weeks prior to the iPhone's release, the plastic screen was replaced with glass. This was after Jobs was upset when he saw that his keys scratched the prototype in his pocket. The fast switch led to a bidding process for a manufacturing contractor that was won by [Foxconn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foxconn), which had just opened up a new wing of its [Shenzhen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shenzhen) factory complex specifically for this bid.[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-21)<sup>[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-22)</sup> Apple partnered with [Corning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corning_Inc.) on the glass.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-i468-23)

## Release and performance

### Initial release

Six out of ten Americans surveyed said they knew before the release that the iPhone was coming.<sup>[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-guardianswarm-24)</sup> The iPhone was released in the United States on June 29, 2007, at the price of $499 for the 4 GB model and $599 for the 8 GB model, both requiring a 2-year contract.<sup>[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-macworldlive-12)</sup> Thousands of people were reported to have waited outside [Apple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Store) and [AT&T](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AT&T) retail stores days before the device's launch;<sup>[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-25)</sup> many stores reported stock shortages within an hour of availability.[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-26)[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-guardianswarm-24)

Sales to the European market started in November 2007,<sup>[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-27)</sup> first in Germany, followed by Britain and then France.<sup>[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-28)</sup> Reports suggested that these launches were met with less enthusiasm.<sup>[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-TS-29)</sup> In France it was sold by [Orange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orange_S.A.) for 649 euros.<sup>[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-SF-30)</sup> The iPhone was released in Austria and the Republic of Ireland on March 13, 2008.[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-31)[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-32)

In Canada, [Rogers Wireless](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogers_Wireless) announced in April 2008 that a deal was reached with Apple to bring the iPhone to the Canadian market.<sup>[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-33)</sup> The original iPhone was eventually not released in Canada in favor of the second-generation [iPhone 3G](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPhone_3G).[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-34)

### Post-release

The iPhone's main competitors in both consumer and business markets were considered to be the [LG Prada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LG_Prada), [LG Viewty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LG_Viewty), [Samsung Ultra Smart F700](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samsung_Ultra_Smart_F700), [Nokia N95](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nokia_N95), [Nokia E61i](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nokia_E61i), [Palm Treo 750](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Treo_750), [Palm Centro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Centro), [HTC Touch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTC_Touch), [Sony Ericsson W960](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Ericsson_W960), [Sony Ericsson C905](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Ericsson_C905) and [BlackBerry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BlackBerry).[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-35)[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-36)[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-37)[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-38)

#### Price drops and revisions

The [iPod Touch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPod_Touch), a touchscreen device with the media and internet abilities and interface of the iPhone but without the ability to connect to a cellular network for phone functions or internet access, was released on September 5, 2007. At the same time, Apple significantly dropped the price of the iPhone 8 GB model from $599 to $399 (still requiring a 2-year contract with AT&T) while discontinuing the $499 4 GB model.<sup>[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-39)</sup> After receiving "hundreds of emails" upset about the price drop, Apple gave a $100 store credit to early adopters.[\[39\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-40)

A 16 GB model was released on February 5, 2008, for $499, the original launch price of the 4 GB model.<sup>[\[40\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-41)</sup> Apple released an [SDK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IOS_SDK) on March 6, 2008, allowing developers to create the apps that would be available starting in iPhone OS [version 2.0](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IOS_version_history), a free upgrade for iPhone users. On June 9, Apple announced the [iPhone 3G](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPhone_3G), which began shipping July 11.[\[41\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-42)

### Sales

In its first week, Apple sold 270,000 iPhones domestically.<sup>[\[42\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-CI-43)</sup> Apple sold its one millionth iPhone 74 days after release.<sup>[\[43\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-44)</sup> Apple reported in January 2008 that four million had been sold.<sup>[\[44\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-45)</sup> By Q4 2007, strong iPhone sales put Apple at second place among U.S. smartphone vendors, behind [Research In Motion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BlackBerry_Limited) and ahead of all [Windows Mobile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_Mobile) vendors.[\[45\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-46)

By October 2007, the iPhone was the fourth-best-selling handset in the U.S., trailing the [Motorola Razr V3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motorola_Razr_V3), the [LG Chocolate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LG_Chocolate), and the [LG VX8300](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LG_VX8300).[\[46\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-47)

Compared to the United States,[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-TS-29)<sup>[\[42\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-CI-43)</sup> European sales were "sluggish".<sup>[\[47\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-48)</sup> Although Apple partners called its British weekend launch successful, the *[Register](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Register)* called it a "flop".<sup>[\[48\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-49)</sup> According to an analyst, iPhone per-capita sales were one quarter that of the United States<sup>[\[49\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-50)</sup> and it was reportedly outsold by the [LG Viewty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LG_Viewty).<sup>[\[50\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-51)</sup> In France, the device reportedly sold 30,000 units in its first week,<sup>[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-SF-30)</sup> three times as many as were sold in Germany (10,000).[\[42\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-CI-43)[\[51\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-52)

The original iPhone was discontinued on July 11, 2008; total sales volume came to 6,124,000 units.<sup>\[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed)*\]</sup> It was the first model to be neither released nor discontinued in September unlike the [iPhone 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPhone_4) and later, however the [iPhone 8 and 8 Plus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPhone_8) as well as the [iPhone 14 and 14 Plus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPhone_14_and_14_Plus) were discontinued earlier than September.

## Reception and legacy

### Critical reception

The iPhone received largely positive reviews. Only four writers were given review models of the iPhone:[\[52\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-53)[\[53\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-54)[David Pogue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Pogue) of *[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times)*,[\[54\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-55)[Walt Mossberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Mossberg) of *[The Wall Street Journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wall_Street_Journal)*,[\[55\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-56)[Steven Levy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Levy) of *[Newsweek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newsweek)*,<sup>[\[56\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-57)</sup> and [Ed Baig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Baig) of *[USA Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA_Today)*.[\[57\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-58)*The New York Times* and *The Wall Street Journal* published positive, but cautious, reviews of the iPhone, their primary criticisms being the relatively slow speed of [AT&T](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AT&T)'s 2.5G [EDGE](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EDGE_(telecommunication)>) network and the phone's inability to connect using [3G](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3G) services. *The Wall Street Journal*'s technology columnist, Walt Mossberg, concluded that "despite some flaws and feature omissions, the iPhone is, on balance, a beautiful and breakthrough handheld computer."[\[58\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-59)*[Time](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_(magazine)>)* magazine named it the Invention of the Year in 2007.[\[59\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-60)

The British publication Mobile Phones UK (later S21) reviewed the iPhone upon its local launch in November 2007 and gave it a rating of 5 out of 5, having been "blown away" by the phone's user interface. However the review was lambasted by many readers who felt that it was unbalanced. Taking the feedback on board, the site revised the rating to a final 3 out of 5, commenting "With hindsight, 5 stars was wrong."<sup>[\[60\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-61)</sup> Another UK-based publication, *Mobile Gazette*, wrote that "Although it has many good points, the list of bad points is equally impressive." It also added "Although the iPhone sold well in the US, when it finally hit Europe sales were not as high as expected, to an extent because European consumers could understand the drawbacks due to a more competitive marketplace."[\[61\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-62)*Ars Technica* wrote an early review as well, in which it expresses optimism for the technology, the touchscreen experience, the web browsing and the music player functionality, but also highlights the lack of some features like GPS, a decent email client, limited connectivity and no third-party SDK.[\[62\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:0-63)

[Steve Ballmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Ballmer), the former CEO of Microsoft, argued in 2007 that the first-generation iPhone “is the most expensive phone in the world and it doesn't have a keyboard”, and argued that the 1st gen iPhone was too expensive even with a carrier subsidy and a carrier plan.[\[63\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-64)

### Legacy

The iPhone was the first of the long-running [iPhone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPhone) line of products that continue to this day, which helped Apple to become one of the world's [most valuable companies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_companies_by_revenue).<sup>[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-OL-11)</sup> The first generation iPhone's successor, [iPhone 3G](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPhone_3G), was announced on June 9, 2008.[\[64\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-65)<sup>[\[65\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-66)</sup> On the same day, Apple also introduced the [App Store](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/App_Store_(Apple)>) which allowed established companies and startup developers to build careers and earn money, via the platform, while providing retail consumers with new ways to access information and connect with other people.[\[66\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-67)

More broadly, the release of the iPhone was the beginning of a shift of smartphones away from the push-button keyboards of the [BlackBerry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BlackBerry) and [Palm Treo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Treo), towards touchscreen-focused designs with minimal front-facing buttons, mimicking the iPhone. While the [LG Prada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LG_Prada), a [feature phone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feature_phone) with a large [capacitative touchscreen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capacitative_touchscreen), was released in March 2007, the iPhone was the first large-touchscreen phone with multi-touch and with full mobile rendering of websites, features which have now become virtually universal in smartphones. (The last push-button successor of the Treo, the [HP Veer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HP_Veer), was discontinued in 2011, and the BlackBerry was sold off by parent company [BlackBerry Limited](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BlackBerry_Limited) in 2016 before being discontinued in 2020. Since then, the only smartphones with push-button keyboards have been niche products such as [Unihertz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unihertz) phones.) It also marked the beginning of the massive growth of the smartphone market, which expanded from the business and other professional users who had been the predominant users of the BlackBerry to include the general public.[\[67\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-68)

While it was marketed as a [smartphone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smartphone) by Apple, a number of publications at the time and in retrospect have stated that the first generation iPhone was in essence not a smartphone due to the fact that it did not feature the ability to [install](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Installation_(computer_programs)>) third-party apps.[\[68\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-NS-69)[\[69\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-70)<sup>[\[70\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-71)</sup> The technology market intelligence firm ABI Research had stated, after the iPhone's announcement: "we must conclude at this point that based on our current definition of a smartphone that the Apple iPhone is *not* a smartphone. It is a very high-end [feature phone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feature_phone)."<sup>[\[71\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-72)</sup> The App Store download marketplace, which opened a third-party ecosystem, did not release until the next year alongside the second generation iPhone, iPhone 3G.[\[68\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-NS-69)

In July 2023, an unopened, first edition model of the 2007 4 GB iPhone was sold at auction in the US for $190,372.80, nearly 400 times the original price.[\[72\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-73)

## Hardware

The iPhone's back cover is made out of [aluminum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aluminum), a soft metal.<sup>[\[73\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-74)</sup> The iPhone's screen is a 320×480-resolution [LCD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquid-crystal_display) screen at 163 [ppi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pixel_density) that measures about 3.5 inches (89 mm) diagonally, much bigger than most other phones at the time, and the iPhone was the first mobile phone with [multi-touch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multi-touch) technology. The screen's refresh rate is 60 [Hz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hz). The rear camera on the iPhone has a resolution of 2 [megapixels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pixel) and also features [geotagging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geotagged_photograph). The iPhone has four total buttons and a single switch: a power and sleep button, a volume up and volume down button, a silent/ringer switch, and a home button positioned in the bottom center of the face of the phone. The home button, when pressed, would send the user back to the [home screen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_screen) from whatever app they were currently using.

The iPhone features a [Samsung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samsung) [32-bit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/32-bit) [ARM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ARM_architecture) [microprocessor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microprocessor), [underclocked](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Underclocking) from its stock 620 [MHz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hertz) to a slower 412 MHz to increase battery life.[\[74\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-Processor-75)<sup>[\[75\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-76)</sup> Its GPU is the [PowerVR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PowerVR) [MBX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PowerVR#MBX) Lite 3D.[\[76\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-77)

The iPhone also includes several sets of sensors, including an [accelerometer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accelerometer), a [proximity sensor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proximity_sensor), and an [ambient light sensor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photodetector). Similar to the [iPod Touch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPod_Touch), the iPhone also features a 3.5 millimeter auxiliary headphone jack. The phone has a 3.7 V 1400 [mAh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MAh) [lithium-ion battery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithium-ion_battery) built in it.

## Software

At the time of its unveiling in January, Steve Jobs claimed: "iPhone runs [OS X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OS_X)" and runs "desktop-class applications",[\[77\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-78)<sup>[\[78\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-79)</sup> but at the time of the iPhone's release, the operating system was renamed "iPhone OS".[\[79\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-80)

The original iPhone supported three major versions of the operating system before it was discontinued: [iPhone OS 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPhone_OS_1), [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPhone_OS_2), and [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPhone_OS_3). The last update the original iPhone received was iPhone OS 3.1.3, as [iPhone OS 3.2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IOS_version_history#iPhone_OS_3) was intended for [the iPad](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPad_(1st_generation)>).

### Software history

The original operating system for the original iPhone, [iPhone OS 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPhone_OS_1), featured [Visual Voicemail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visual_Voicemail), [multi-touch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multi-touch) gestures, [HTML email](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTML_email), Apple's [Safari](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safari_(web_browser)>) web browser, [threaded](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conversation_threading) [text messaging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Text_messaging), a music and video player app named "iPod" (its features would later be included in the [Music](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_(app)>) and [Apple TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_TV_App) apps), a dedicated [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube) [app](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube#Platforms) and a [Maps app](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Maps#Mobile_app) powered by [Google Maps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Maps), however without proper GPS support.<sup>[\[62\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-:0-63)</sup> It also included basic Phone/contacts, Calendar, Photos, Stocks, Weather, Clock, Calculator, Notes, and Settings apps. However, many features like [MMS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multimedia_Messaging_Service), [apps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobile_app), and [copy and paste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cut,_copy,_and_paste) were not supported at release, leading hackers to [jailbreak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IOS_jailbreaking) their phones to add these features. By jailbreaking, it was also possible to overcome the lack of a native GPS module with the [Navizon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navizon) app, which used WiFi and cell-tower positioning, to give users access to real time location, otherwise impossible.<sup>[\[80\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-81)</sup> Software updates from Apple gradually added these functions.

A v1.1 update alongside the introduction of the [iPod Touch](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPod_Touch_(1st_generation)>) in September 2007 included an [iTunes Store](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITunes_Store) app that was the first new app to be added to the system.[\[81\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-82)

[iPhone OS 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPhone_OS_2) was released on July 11, 2008, at the same time as the release of the [iPhone 3G](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPhone_3G), and introduced Apple's [App Store](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/App_Store_(Apple)>) supporting native third-party applications (that were developed with the [iPhone SDK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPhone_SDK)), [Microsoft Exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Exchange_Server) support,[\[82\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-83)[push e-mail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Push_e-mail), and other enhancements.

[iPhone OS 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPhone_OS_3) was released on June 17, 2009, alongside the [iPhone 3GS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPhone_3GS), and introduced copy and paste support, [Spotlight search](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotlight_(Apple)>) for the [home screen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpringBoard), and new features for the [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube) app. iPhone OS 3 was available for the original iPhone as well as the iPhone 3G and 3GS. However, not all features of iPhone OS 3 (such as [MMS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multimedia_Messaging_Service) in the [Messages](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Messages_(Apple)>) app) were supported on the original iPhone.

iPhone OS 3.1.3 was the last version of iPhone OS (now [iOS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IOS)) to be released for the phone in February 2010,<sup>[\[83\]](https://en.wikipedia.org#cite_note-84)</sup> which never got the full iPhone OS 3 feature set because [iPhone OS 3.2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IOS_version_history#iPhone_OS_3) was intended for [the iPad](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPad_(1st_generation)>).

Almost all apps released after the release of iOS 6 in late September 2012 do not run on the original iPhone, as the software development kit (SDK) was changed to no longer allow the "targeting" (minimum) of iOS versions older than 4.3 (including 3.x), or ARMv6 devices (first two generations).

## FAQs about the first iPhone

### When did the first iPhone come out?

The iPhone was announced on January 9, 2007, and went on sale in the U.S. on June 29, 2007.

### How much did the first iPhone cost?

The iPhone launched at $499 for the 4GB model and $599 for the 8GB model.

### When did Apple cut the price of the first iPhone?

Apple lowered the price of the 8GB iPhone from $599 to $399 on September 5, 2007. That was a $200 price drop a little more than two months after launch.

### Did the first iPhone have an App Store?

No. The original iPhone did not have an App Store at launch. The App Store launched in 2008 with 500 apps.

### What storage sizes did the first iPhone have?

The iPhone came in 4GB and 8GB storage options at launch.

### Did the first iPhone have a camera?

Yes. The original iPhone had a 2-megapixel rear camera. It could take still photos, but it did not support video recording.

### Did the first iPhone support 5G?

No. The iPhone came long before 5G. It supported GSM, EDGE, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth 2.0.

### Did the first iPhone have Siri?

No. Siri was not available on the original iPhone. Voice assistant features came to iPhone years later.

### What were the first iPhone’s biggest limitations?

Some of the most-cited limitations were no App Store at launch, no 3G, no video recording, no MMS, no copy and paste, and limited customization compared with today’s iPhones.

### How does the first iPhone compare with iPhone 18 Pro?

The original iPhone focused on calls, music, web browsing, email, maps, photos, and Visual Voicemail. iPhone 18 Pro adds the A20 Pro chip, a 48MP Fusion Main camera with variable aperture plus 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide and Telephoto cameras, a 6.3-inch (or 6.9-inch on iPhone 18 Pro Max) Super Retina XDR display with ProMotion, up to 36 hours of video playback (up to 45 hours on iPhone 18 Pro Max), Apple Intelligence with Siri AI, and modern 5G connectivity.

### How does the first iPhone compare with iPhone Duo?

The original iPhone had one fixed 3.5-inch touchscreen. iPhone Duo uses a foldable design with a 7.6-inch inner display, a 5.4-inch outer display, a 48MP Fusion Main camera with an integrated 2x Telephoto, and Split View multitasking, giving users more screen space in a device designed to stay portable.

## How far we’ve come

If the original iPhone was like a digital Swiss Army knife, today’s models are more like pocket-sized supercomputers. They’re sleek, powerful, and packed with tools that were once unthinkable on a mobile device.

The first iPhone gave people a phone, an iPod, and an internet communicator in one device. Today, iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo add advanced cameras, larger displays, 5G, AI features, stronger privacy tools, and new ways to work, create, and communicate.

So, what can we expect from Apple iPhones as we look ahead to the next decade or two? No one's exactly sure yet. But you can bet we'll be looking back and laughing about what we didn't have.
